title: Water, Soil and Renewable Resources
seo_title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science: Water, Soil and Renewable Resources Worksheets
standard_code: Earth and Environmental Science Unit 3: Use of renewable Earth resources
standard_text: Renewable resources and sustainable yield; groundwater, aquifers, porosity and permeability; the Great Artesian Basin and Murray–Darling Basin; soil formation, erosion and salinity; solar, wind, hydro and geothermal energy and energy storage. (Senior Secondary Earth and Environmental Science, Unit 3: Living on Earth – extracting, using and managing Earth resources)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science worksheets on renewable resources: groundwater, aquifers, porosity, the Great Artesian Basin, soil erosion, salinity, solar, wind and pumped hydro. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Renewable only if used no faster than it is replaced.
key_sub: Porosity stores water; permeability lets it flow.
body_html:
How to think about it

A resource is renewable if natural processes replace it as fast as it is used. Water, soil, forests and fish can all be overused. Groundwater fills the pores of aquifers; porosity is the space for water and permeability how easily it flows. The Great Artesian Basin supplies much of inland Australia.

Soil forms very slowly from weathered rock and organic matter but is quickly lost by erosion; clearing can also cause dryland salinity. Solar, wind and hydro energy are renewable, but their output varies, so storage such as batteries and pumped hydro (Snowy 2.0) is needed.

Example

Recharge 50 GL/yr, extraction 70 GL/yr. Water table?

extraction > recharge

Answer: falls by 20 GL of storage each year

Example

A 5 kW solar system gives 20 kWh/day. Mean output hours at full power?

20 ÷ 5

Answer: 4 hours

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a porous rock must be permeable (clay is porous but not permeable).
  • Calling all water renewable no matter how fast it is used.
  • Saying solar panels work at full output at night.
